info.name: TOMP-API Sandbox
info.description:
Drives the TOMP-API v2 sandbox server (see ../README.md) through a full, real package/leg lifecycle: search offers, purchase, confirm, start/end a leg, pay and settle - plus rollback/cancel alternatives and negative/error-path checks.

Run the whole collection top-to-bottom (Collection Runner, or `newman run TOMP-API-Sandbox.postman_collection.json`) against a running sandbox (`npm start` in ../, default http://localhost:4010). Folders execute in order:

1. Auth - gets a Bearer token used by every later request (collection-level auth)
2. Health
3. Happy Path Lifecycle - the full search -> purchase -> confirm -> execute -> pay -> settle flow, searching from Amsterdam Centraal so the default (`gosharing`) provider's own offer shows up alongside the walking one
4. Alternative Flows - rollback and cancel, each fetching/purchasing its own fresh offer first so they don't disturb the happy-path package
5. Error Scenarios - 401/404/409/501/400, the last two of which reuse state left behind by folder 3
6. Compare Providers (multi-instance) - run `../start-providers.ps1` or `../start-providers.sh` first, then this folder queries each running instance directly by port to show the *same* search returning a different operator's offer (or none, outside its coverage) depending which one you ask. Reuses the token from folder 1 - every instance accepts it as long as they share the sandbox's default JWT secret.

request.description: No Authorization header at all -> 401 in the TOMP error envelope.
No package with this id has ever been created -> 404.
Depends on folder 02 having run first: {{packageId}} is now SETTLED, so confirming it again is an illegal transition -> 409.
extend-leg is a valid legOperation per the spec's enum, but is out of scope for this sandbox -> 501.
inputs.offer is required by the spec's requestBody schema -> 400 (caught by express-openapi-validator).

item.name: 05 - Compare Providers (multi-instance)
item.description: Needs several sandbox instances running first - `../start-providers.ps1` (Windows) or `../start-providers.sh` (bash), which by default bring up gosharing/uber/check/viavan on :4010-:4013. Every request here targets one instance directly by port instead of {{baseUrl}}, reusing the token from folder 00 (all instances accept it as long as they share the default JWT secret). Deselect this folder in Collection Runner (or skip it with newman's `--folder`) if you're only running a single instance - its requests will fail to connect otherwise.
